image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of a Blenheim spaniel lying in green grass. The dog is positioned on the right side of the frame, facing slightly left. It has characteristic white fur with rich chestnut/red patches on its ears and around one eye. The background features blurred greenery and pink flowers, indicating a shallow depth of field.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape is visible; the dome is apparent, and the muzzle is short with a distinct stop. The nose appears black and appropriately sized.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible eye is dark, round, and expressive. The spacing appears consistent with the breed standard, though only one eye is fully clear due to the angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ear on the right is clearly visible, showing long, wavy/feathered hair typical of the breed. The set appears low on the skull.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coat pattern matches the 'Blenheim' description perfectly: white base with distinct chestnut/red markings on the ears and face.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture appears soft and silky. Feathering is visible on the ears and the front leg/chest area resting on the grass.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a close-up crop focusing on the head and front shoulders. The full body, back length, and overall 'cobby' proportion cannot be verified as the rear half is out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are straight with fine bone and feathered hindquarters.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the front paws/legs are partially visible. Hindquarters and the full structure of the legs are not in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is docked and carried level with back, well-feathered.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame.
The dog is lying down (static pose), so gait cannot be evaluated.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The transition between the white fur of the front paw and the grass blades is slightly soft and indistinct. Some grass blades appear to merge into the fur rather than sitting distinctly on top or behind it, suggesting minor segmentation or generation blending issues.

The background blur is very uniform and painterly, which is common in AI images but also mimics optical bokeh. It is not severe enough to be an artifact on its own but contributes to a slight 'digital' feel.
